1. Overview — The ABpE Module System

1.1 What is a Module?

The ABpE Portal is completely modular. Every function — CV Editor, Admin Portal, Documentation — is an independent module. A module bundles everything it needs:

  • Configuration — module.json (required)
  • Template — HTML file(s)
  • CSS — Module-specific styles (optional)
  • JavaScript — Module logic (optional)
  • Translations — JSON language files (optional)

The most important thing: No modification of views.py or urls.py required. The system automatically detects new modules.

1.2 The ModuleScanner

The ModuleScanner (apps/abpe_ui/core/module_scanner.py) runs at Django startup and scans all subdirectories under:

apps/abpe_ui/templates/abpe_ui/modules/

Every folder containing a module.json is recognized as a module and added to the navigation. The order is determined by the order field in the module.json.

1.3 The Generic View

The function module_view() in views.py handles routing for all modules generically:

# urls.py — at the very bottom (after all specific routes)
path('<str:module_id>/',                views.module_view, name='module'),
path('<str:module_id>/<str:subpage>/', views.module_view, name='module_subpage')

The view reads the module.json of the requested module, checks permissions, and renders the appropriate template. The context automatically contains active_module, current_lang, module_config, and the complete navigation.

1.4 Lifecycle of a Request

  1. Browser calls /my_module/
  2. Django matches the generic route <str:module_id>/
  3. module_view() looks for templates/abpe_ui/modules/my_module/module.json
  4. Permission check (roles, DB overrides)
  5. Template is rendered with full context
  6. Browser loads Core-CSS → Core-JS → Module-CSS → Module-JS
  7. loadLanguage() loads language files and applies data-i18n
